# libs/web/core/auth

Session state, token refresh and route guards (PRD sections 5.3 and 7.2).

- `SessionService` is the only owner of the session: `status`, `isAuthenticated` and `accessToken` are signals; `login`, `register`, `logout`, `refresh` and `restore` change them.
- The access token lives only in memory. The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie on the web and lives in `SECURE_STORAGE` on native apps (`RefreshTokenStore`, MOB-12). Never put tokens in `KEY_VALUE_STORAGE` or `localStorage`.
- `refresh()` is single-flight: parallel callers share one request (FE-14). `authInterceptor` refreshes on `TOKEN_EXPIRED`, retries each request once (`RETRIED_AFTER_REFRESH`) and never touches requests marked with `SKIP_AUTH`.
- Only `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` ends the session. A network failure keeps the stored token and retries when the network comes back, so an offline start does not sign the user out (MOB-10). Resume from the background refreshes an expired token (MOB-6).
- Guards are `CanMatchFn` (`authGuard`, `guestGuard`). In functional guards call every `inject()` before the first `await`; after it the injection context is gone.
- Tests: `src/lib/testing.spec-helpers.ts` sets up the real interceptors, `HttpTestingController` and the platform fakes; `settle()` lets promise chains reach the next request.
